intended_object: This is the integrand x ↦ e^{-2πi⟨n,x⟩}·exp(-a‖Σ xᵢ bᵢ‖²) on ℝ^ι, i.e. the Gaussian in lattice-basis coordinates multiplied by a Fourier character. The library uses it as a helper in the Poisson-summation step of its Odlyzko-bound proof. I inferred this from the docstring ("used in the Odlyzko-bound argument") and from how the file uses it.
explanation: The body multiplies `coordinateFourierCharacter n x`, which is `mFourier (-n)` evaluated at the image of x in the torus, by `coordinateGaussian L b a x`, which is the lattice Gaussian of the point with coordinates x in the basis b. Its only role is in proofs. In `mFourierCoeff_gaussianTorusPeriodization` it is the integrand whose integral over ℝ^ι gives the n-th Fourier coefficient of the periodized Gaussian. In `coordinateFourierGaussian_eq_ambient` it is rewritten as an ambient Fourier-Gaussian evaluated at the dual-lattice point, after which its integral is computed. It is an intermediate expression bundled for the library's internal use in one proof, not a standard mathematical object with a counterpart in the literature or in Mathlib. As an expression it is correct: the product of the Fourier character with the coordinate Gaussian is exactly the integrand that defines the Fourier coefficient.
